fills.BRANCH_MODEL: One worktree per session under `.claude/worktrees/`, one branch per change off `main`. A session spawned from a chip starts in one; otherwise create it with `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<topic> -b <topic> main`. Work only there: the main checkout takes only merges, deploys and `claude:install`. A worktree without its own `node_modules` resolves packages from the main checkout's, which follows main's `package.json`: when the branch's dependencies differ, run `npm install` in the worktree. Uncommitted changes outside your worktree belong to another session: don't stage them, ask about them or mention them. Stage explicit paths only. The branch's label (ui, server, data, integration, ops, docs, fix, refactor, research) picks its gates in phase 4.
fills.DESIGN_AUTHORITY: the window's existing screens under `web/src` (there are no mockups: match the neighbouring components, `web/src/styles.css`, and the keyboard conventions in `web/src/useKeyboard.ts`)
fills.FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS: `npm run deploy`, `npm run claude:install` or `npm run claude:uninstall`; never read or write `~/.inprogress` or the live InProgress server on 4317 (tests run against `.test-home` and `.test-claude`)
fills.MERGE_GATE:
On Aiden's go-ahead only; it drops the `REVIEW` prefix (Session title, below). If `main` moved, merge it into the branch in its worktree first and rerun the checks. Then, from the main checkout: `git merge --no-ff <branch>`, then `npm run deploy` (typecheck and unit always; smoke and e2e when the changed files need them; a red deploy means fix on the branch, merge and deploy again, and `npm run rollback` swaps the previous live build back), then `npm run claude:install` when the branch touched `claude/` or `src/hooks/`. Then push `main` with the personal account's token and leave the active gh account alone:

```bash
git -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo password=$(gh auth token --user Aiden-Molyneaux); }; f' push origin main
```

A PR only when Aiden asks. Deploy and `claude:install` never run from a worktree: the installed hooks bake in the main checkout's absolute path.

Once `main` is pushed, brief the scribe that the step is done with its outcome, and prefix this session's title with `DONE` (Session title, below).

A deploy or rollback that goes red on the environment (a lock, a restart, the runner) goes to Doctor Nick before anything is retried; a red typecheck or test is the work, fixed on the branch. A retry that is itself a
gated action (another deploy, a rollback, an installer) follows the gate above.
fills.PLAN_HOME: `docs/superpowers/plans/`, specs in `docs/superpowers/specs/`, and provisional rulings and open questions in `docs/superpowers/rulings/`
fills.PREFLIGHT:
Two modes, by what the work runs against:

- **The live install** (this session's hooks, the scribe, the window on 4317; the main session
  only): `node C:/personal/InProgress/dist/cli/main.js doctor`. It checks, in order: Server,
  Token, Database, Hooks, Scribe agent, Skill, Allow rules, MCP server, and Edge. No ✗ line, or
  its printed fix applied and the doctor rerun, before going on. A `!` line is a warning (Edge
  missing, the hooks on another Node, MCP skipped): act on it only when it bears on the work.
- **An isolated build** (Parvati, Sev on a UI plan, a hand-driven check of a branch): from the
  worktree, `node scripts/build-to.mjs .build`, then start `.build/dist/server/main.js` the way
  `test/e2e/start-server.mjs` does (`INPROGRESS_HOME` set to a scratch folder,
  `INPROGRESS_PORT` set to the lane port, `INPROGRESS_AGENT_WATCH_MS=500`), and confirm
  `GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/health` answers with `"app":"inprogress"` before driving it.
  Ports 4400 to 4419 only (Parvati 4400 to 4409, Sev's e2e 4410 to 4419), never 4317 or 4399,
  and never `~/.inprogress`. `npm run test:e2e` does all of this itself on
  `INPROGRESS_E2E_PORT`.
fills.PROTECTED_LANES:
The live server on 4317 and `~/.inprogress` hold every project's tree, and every session's
  hooks read them: a triage never stops, restarts or edits them without saying so.
  `node C:/personal/InProgress/dist/cli/main.js stop` only when a fix needs it, named in
  the receipt, and then `start` yourself. Otherwise it stays down until something starts it (a new
  session, the scribe's MCP server, `start`, `doctor`, `open`, a deploy or rollback); until then the
  window is dark and every open session's hooks fail into `hooks.log`. `npm run deploy`, `npm run rollback` and `npm run claude:install`
  run only from the main checkout and only under Sigmund's merge gate (phase 8), never as a
  triage step.
fills.RISK_STATEMENT: `~/.inprogress` and the live window are unrecoverable: the live database holds every project's tree and resources, every Claude session on this machine reads it through the installed hooks, and no git revert undoes a stray write there or a bad deploy.
fills.RUNBOOK:
| Symptom | First probe | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The doctor prints a ✗ line | The line itself | Its printed fix, then rerun the doctor. A printed `inprogress <cmd>` means `node C:/personal/InProgress/dist/cli/main.js <cmd>`, and when a printed fix says `stop` (some add "the next session starts the new build"), run `start` straight after it yourself |
| The doctor prints a `!` line | Whether it bears on the work (Edge only matters for `open`; another Node only after an nvm switch) | Its printed fix when it does; otherwise note it and go on |
| A session started with no InProgress briefing, or `tasks` says InProgress is not running | `node C:/personal/InProgress/dist/cli/main.js status`, then the tail of `~/.inprogress/hooks.log` and `~/.inprogress/server.log` | Known issue: the server is not running when a hook fires |
| `EPERM`, `EBUSY` or `EACCES` on a rename, a folder move, an install or a deploy | What holds the handle: the live server (files under the main checkout's `node_modules`), an editor, a shell sitting in the folder, antivirus | Known issue: Windows file locks |
| `npm run deploy` or `npm run rollback` ends red | The last `▸` step it printed, and whether it printed "rolling back" | Known issue: a red deploy or rollback |
| `Cannot find module`, or a package missing, in a worktree | Is the missing module the repo's own `dist/...`? Then a command ran a relative path from a worktree, which has no `dist/`: use `node C:/personal/InProgress/dist/cli/main.js`. Otherwise, does the worktree have its own `node_modules`? Each one here keeps its own; without it, Node resolves from the main checkout's, which follows main's `package.json`, not the branch's | The absolute path, or `npm install` in the worktree |
| Hooks behave like an unmerged build, or the doctor's Hooks line says a hook script no longer exists | The hook entries in `~/.claude/settings.json`: each one's `args[0]` (the script; `command` is the Node binary) should start with `C:/personal/InProgress/dist/`, and so should the MCP server path in `~/.claude/agents/inprogress-scribe.md` | Known issue: claude:install from the wrong checkout |
| The first `npm test` run reports a failed file with no failing test | Rerun `npm test` once | Known issue: the first `npm test` run fails a file |
| `npm run dev` does not start or answer | The dev server's own output, and whether another process holds 4318 (`scripts/dev.mjs` runs on 4318 with `.dev-home` as its data) | Close the other process; never point dev at 4317 or `~/.inprogress` |
| An isolated build does not answer on its port | The server's own output, and `/api/health` on that port (another program, or another session's build, may hold it) | The preflight above; on a clash, another port in the lane |
fills.SHIP_POLICY: InProgress has no integration branch, and nothing is pushed before the merge. The branch stays in its worktree until phase 8; Sigmund never pushes a branch to origin, and `main` is pushed only by the gate below. Ask first before anything on the risk list, before a migration, before a deletion, and before growing the scope past the request.

fills.SESSION_RHYTHM:
- You can't see your context size. A hook (`scripts/context-nudge.mjs`) tells you when it crosses 150k and 200k, and `.claude/settings.json` autocompacts at 250k.
- One step, one session: you drive a step from claim to done. A clean point is right after a merge, or after a finished plan task with everything committed in your worktree.
- At the 150k nudge, finish the task you are on, commit, and ask Aiden to run `/compact` with a line naming the plan file, the branch and any open findings. Do not cut the session. Unattended overnight, the same rhythm without stopping: carry on, and the autocompact is the reset. Provisional rulings and open questions go to the rulings file in `docs/superpowers/rulings/`.
- After a compaction the hook says so. Reload this skill, then reread your plan file and the step block before you go on.
- Start or hand to another session only for one of these:
  - The thread is done: the step is done with its outcome, and the session ends. No handoff.
  - Independent parallel pieces on separate files: helper sessions on the same step, which claim without `--take-over`. Sev subagents in the same session stay preferred for mechanical work.
  - Another repo, machine or cloud environment.
  - Scope that splits into a new step: add it through the scribe; it gets its own Sigmund later.
  - A broken session (compaction lost the plan, a loop, a harness crash): a handoff from the plan file.
  - A long wait with a large context (days, over 200k): a handoff costs about what the cold wake would.

  The context nudge, a review wait and a subagent run are never reasons to hand off. A handoff to a successor on the same step opens `Claim #<id> --take-over`, names the worktree (`.claude/worktrees/<topic>`), and lists the step's undelivered answers. Write it, brief the scribe to attach it to its step, print its path, offer the next session as a chip whose prompt is the handoff prompt when the `spawn_task` tool is available (the desktop app), and stop.
- A new request mid-session becomes a queued step through the scribe (`later: #id`, or a new step), unless it is a few lines in code that is already open. The InProgress tree is the memory between sessions.
- Report to Mip through InProgress only: the step's status and outcome, new steps, asks, and the working tasks. Mip reads them at its next opening. Do not message Mip.
- **Session title (Aiden, 2026-10-16, #455).** In the desktop app, keep a status prefix on this session's title so the sidebar shows where it stands:
  - `REVIEW`: set whenever you end a turn with the phase 7 receipt still open, its `review` ask included. The go-ahead ("ship it", "merge it", "go ahead") drops it and phase 8 runs with no prefix; a change request drops it until the next receipt.
  - `BLOCKED`: set when you end a turn waiting on Aiden for anything but the receipt: a scribe `question` or `permission` ask, or a question in your closing message. Drop it when he answers. If one is open while the receipt waits, `BLOCKED` wins: his answer comes before a ship. A question asked inside a turn (AskUserQuestion) sets nothing.
  - `DONE`: set once the step is merged, deployed and pushed (phase 8). It stays.
  - Otherwise no prefix: while you work, deploy retries included.

  A session that hands off clears its prefix before it stops; the successor sets its own. Read the title with `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_session` on `"self"`, then set it with `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_title` on `"self"`: one prefix and a space before the title as it stands, replacing any prefix already there (`REVIEW #453 Filter the Backlog`, then `DONE #453 Filter the Backlog`). Load both through ToolSearch when they are deferred. Only the main session renames: a subagent cannot rename the session it runs in. Where the tools are missing (outside the desktop app) or a rename is declined, skip it without comment.
